acceptance:
  - claim: >-
      `citations_held_at` (`saffron/spec_citations.py:449-461`) reads the
      suffix set `_extract_citations` tokenizes against from `tokens_at`'s
      tree whenever it is given, the same tree `citation_count_and_defects`
      reads its own suffix set from at the commit it checks
      (`saffron/spec_citations.py:350-351`). The one committed witness for
      this, `test_a_bare_citation_is_held_by_the_file_the_later_check_anchors_it_to`,
      drives only a suffix a later commit adds. This criterion drives the
      other direction: a root-level suffix the spec's own commit carries,
      which the later commit has already dropped. At the spec's own
      commit, with `tokens_at` set to that later commit, the bare citation
      reads as anchored to the same path the later check anchors it to,
      not to the file whose suffix is gone there, and its construct there
      does not hold the cited range. `rewrite_moved_citations` then leaves
      that defect rather than moving it onto a construct of the same name

  - claim: >-
      `_stack_cite`'s callable (`saffron/cli.py:1306-1322`) passes the
      same commit, `head`, as both the commit `citation_defects` checks
      (`saffron/cli.py:1321`) and the `tokens_at` `citations_held_at`
      reads (`saffron/cli.py:1317-1320`), so the two already cannot
      disagree about which backtick tokens are paths. The witness drives
      a real mirror where the queued spec's own commit carries a
      root-level file with a unique suffix that a later commit, the one
      `head` resolves to, has already removed. The held map `_stack_cite`
      returns is empty for that citation, not a name sourced from the
      removed file, and `rewrite_moved_citations` leaves the defect
      `citation_defects` reports at `head` rather than moving it.
    witness: tests/test_cli.py::test_a_stack_cites_held_map_does_not_misattribute_a_removed_suffixs_citation
    mutant:
      file: saffron/spec_citations.py
      find: |2
            names_in_tree = _tree_names(mirror, commit)
            token_tree = names_in_tree if tokens_at is None else _tree_names(mirror, tokens_at)
            suffixes = {Path(n).suffix for n in token_tree if Path(n).suffix}
      replace: |2
            names_in_tree = _tree_names(mirror, commit)
            suffixes = {Path(n).suffix for n in names_in_tree if Path(n).suffix}
    wrong_versions:
      - "`citations_held_at` reads `commit`'s own tree for `suffixes` regardless of `tokens_at`, so `_stack_cite`'s held map carries a name sourced from the file `head` no longer carries."
      - "`token_tree` takes the union of `commit`'s suffixes and `tokens_at`'s, so `_stack_cite`'s held map still treats the removed root file as a path."
      - "`tokens_at` governs `suffixes` only when its tree is a superset of `commit`'s, so `_stack_cite`'s held map falls back to `commit`'s own, larger suffix set."
  - claim: >-

      this change.

    preserves: true
  - claim: >-
      `test_a_stack_batchs_citation_check_returns_the_text_it_checked`
      keeps asserting the same patched calls and return values after this
      change.
    witness: tests/test_cli.py::test_a_stack_batchs_citation_check_returns_the_text_it_checked

## Context

This spec grows out of `SA-0321`, already landed at `a013119a` and
amended by its own review at `3d437b44`. Every line cited below was read
at that review commit, which is `HEAD` at the time of writing.

A finding against this stack reads: `citations_held_at` recomputes
`suffixes` from its own `commit`'s tree while `citation_defects`
recomputes `suffixes` independently from `head`'s tree, so a suffix that
enters or leaves the tree between a spec's own commit and the batch's
head can tokenize the same text two different ways, and the held map's
offsets can then name the wrong file for a citation whose shape changed.

That finding's own line citations, checked against this stack's history,
land exactly on `saffron/cli.py:1314` and `:1318` and
`saffron/spec_citations.py:462` and `:353-354` at `a013119a`, the commit
before `SA-0321`'s review, not at `3d437b44`. At `a013119a`,
`citations_held_at` took no `tokens_at` parameter at all and read
`suffixes` from `commit`'s own tree alone
(`git show a013119a:saffron/spec_citations.py` lines 452-463). The
review at `3d437b44` added `tokens_at`, and `_stack_cite`'s callable
(`saffron/cli.py:1287-1322`) already passes `head` as `tokens_at`
whenever it checks a queued spec's citations
(`saffron/cli.py:1316-1320`), the same commit it passes to
`citation_defects` three lines later (`saffron/cli.py:1321`). Since both
calls then read `suffixes` from the same tree, `_extract_citations`
(`saffron/spec_citations.py:210-218`) tokenizes the same text the same
way for both, by construction, and the finding's described mismatch
cannot occur through this caller. `citations_held_at` is called nowhere
else in `saffron/` (`git grep citations_held_at`).

The review's own test,
`test_a_bare_citation_is_held_by_the_file_the_later_check_anchors_it_to`
(`tests/test_spec_citations.py:756-795`), proves this for one direction:
a suffix (`.rs`) that a later commit adds, absent from the spec's own
commit. No committed test builds the other direction, a suffix the
spec's own commit carries that a later commit has already dropped, the
direction a real repo meets when a file type last used in some older
commit disappears before a batch's head. Run by hand against a
constructed repo of that shape, today's `citations_held_at` already
returns the correct, empty held map for it, because `tokens_at` governs
`suffixes` unconditionally rather than only when the tree grows. That
leaves a correctness property proven in code but not locked in by any
witness, and an asymmetric "fix" that only ever widens the suffix set
would pass the one committed test while still failing this direction
silently.

## Problem

Add the missing direction's witness, at both the level that resolves it
(`citations_held_at`) and the level that calls it
(`cli._stack_cite`), and make the existing docstring state the contract
`tokens_at` is meant to uphold.

**The unit witness.** Build a repository with two commits. The first
("own") holds `mod/a.py` defining `thing` at lines 4-5 (padded by three
blank lines) and a root file `x.rs` defining `thing` at lines 1-2. The
second ("head") removes `x.rs`; `mod/a.py` is unchanged. The text is one
paragraph: "The module `mod/a.py` and `x.rs` hold `thing` at `:1-2`." At
`head`, `.rs` is absent from the tree, so `x.rs` is not path-shaped, and
the bare `:1-2` anchors to `mod/a.py` instead, whose `thing` sits at 4-5,
a defect. With no `tokens_at`, `citations_held_at` at "own" still reads
`.rs` from "own"'s own tree, anchors the bare citation to `x.rs`, finds
its `thing` at exactly 1-2, and wrongly holds it. With `tokens_at=head`,
it anchors to `mod/a.py` instead, as `citation_defects` does at `head`,
finds `mod/a.py`'s `thing` at 4-5, which the range 1-2 does not hold, and
holds nothing. `rewrite_moved_citations` then leaves the defect.

**The integration witness.** The same two commits, built directly
through `cli._stack_cite(pinned=pinned)` with `pinned.base_sha` set to
the second commit and no spec-session fakes, since `_stack_cite`'s
callable touches only git and `saffron/spec_citations.py`. The queued
spec file lives at `.saffron/specs/SY-1-x.md` in the first commit and is
untouched by the second. Assert the returned held map is empty and the
returned defect matches `citation_defects`'s own line, then pass both
through `rewrite_moved_citations` and assert the defect is left.

**The docstring.** `citations_held_at`'s docstring
(`saffron/spec_citations.py:452-461`) already names what `tokens_at`
does. Add one sentence stating what passing the wrong commit costs: a
held name can mismatch the file the later check reads.

## Out of scope

- **`saffron/cli.py`.** `_stack_cite` already passes `tokens_at=head`
  correctly. No line there changes.
- **A new caller of `citations_held_at`.** It is called once, by
  `_stack_cite`, today. This spec adds no second caller.
- **The suffix-divergence direction already proven.** Criterion 3
  preserves that witness unchanged.
- **Any change to `rewrite_moved_citations` or `citation_defects`.**
  Neither is touched. Both witnesses call them as committed.

## Notes for the agent

Both mutants are the same edit, reverting `citations_held_at` to read
`suffixes` from `commit`'s own tree regardless of `tokens_at`, which is
exactly how `saffron/spec_citations.py` read it at `a013119a`, before
`SA-0321`'s own review. That one edit kills both witnesses, since
criterion 2's witness calls `cli._stack_cite`, which calls into the same
function.

Build each witness's repository with real commits and the citation
policy `tests/test_spec_citations.py` already uses elsewhere
(`_CITATION_POLICY`), reused as is in `tests/test_spec_citations.py` and
written out directly in `tests/test_cli.py`, which does not import that
constant.

`mod/a.py`'s content is `"\n\n\ndef thing():\n    return 1\n"`, three
blank lines then the two-line function, so its construct sits at lines
4-5 under the committed indentation-based span reader
(`saffron/spec_citations.py:243-249`). `x.rs`'s content is
`"def thing():\n    return 2\n"`, so its construct sits at lines 1-2,
matching the cited range exactly at the commit where it still exists.

Criterion 2's candidate needs no real export directory. Its `path` is
read only for `.name` (`saffron/cli.py:1317`), so any path ending in
`SY-1-x.md` under `tmp_path` is enough.

New prose meets the same ratchet as the rest of this module: no
em dash, semicolon, contraction, perfect tense, or sentence over 25
words. Keep the touched docstring within ten lines total.
